text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet discusses cereals harvest drop and elections.
- Morocco sets up 60,000 election bureaux where voters can pick up their cards.
- Agriculture Minister Hassan Abou Ayoub says bad weather spoilt 60,000 hectares (150,000 acres) of cultivated land.
- Privatisation Minister Abderrahman Saaidi says subscriptions for 20 percent of Imiter silver mine will be opened from June 9 to 13.
- Morocco asks Turkey to withdraw from Iraq.
- Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali and Spanish counterpart Jose Maria Aznar meet in Madrid.
- Moroccan ministers try to get French businessmen to show more interest for investments in the North African country.
- Despite cuts on interest rates, injection of nine billion dirhams ($947 million) in the economy and Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj heartening speeches, investments are sluggish.
